## Product behavior and implementation

`website/app.js` owns the shared scenario and nine views. `engine.js` ports the national operating and finance model in float64. `worker.js` runs named-world calculations without blocking the UI. `scene.js` renders procedural 3D geometry with WebGL2 instancing and a Canvas projection fallback. SVG renders analytical charts and the 2D maps.

The runtime has no npm dependencies or external CDN requirement. Node.js 20+ runs the local server and static copy build. The deployment config sets `npm run build` and `dist`. The original Vite/Three.js suggestion was not a hard requirement; package downloads were restricted, so no installed Three.js runtime is claimed.

The current regional scene shows schematic corridors, hypothetical facility profiles, small aggregate vehicle actors and procedural buildings. Facility interiors include open roof beams, warehouse racks, pallets, sorting/conveyor elements, loading docks, vans and forklift-like actors. Orbit, pan, zoom, reset, pause, speed and timeline controls are present. Actor counts derive from regional demand and selected-hub volume. Display quality changes decorative density only.

Hub capacity, inactive investment candidates, incident-effective daily capacity, variable route costs and nine lane details are exposed through the inspector. The cost layer derives displayed costs from route assumptions and current allocation, rather than hardcoded values. Selecting a national city shows a team-assigned representative market type and its modeled utilization/internal share. It does not invent measured city volumes.

Custom regional current-policy settings preserve 50% internal allocation per zone when capacity permits. Capacity-constrained displaced internal demand is deferred. Non-current policies solve allocation using shared hub and carrier capacities. All demand remains allocated among internal, external, emergency and deferred categories.

Applying the defined Cawang incident resets to its rules 70/88 base policy and central regional operating condition. Cawang loses half capacity for four hours of a twelve-hour day; effective daily capacity is 200,000 instead of 240,000. The four-hour response combines with the unchanged other eight hours. Daily fixed cost is counted once. A single incident does not silently change annual investment cash flows.

The annual JSON export also includes a clearly scoped regional-daily result. CSV has one header row and five national-annual result rows. Imports have a 1MB limit, version checks, a policy whitelist, enum allowlists and numeric bounds. Local saves store bounded settings only. Stale Monte Carlo summaries are hidden when parameter signatures differ.

## Analytical findings that remain binding

Case anchors: 2bn annual parcels; 50% NexExpress/internal; Rp8,000 internal average and Rp12,000 external average; implied Rp20tn logistics spend; Rp5tn 2025 group operating profit. The group P&L residual is not automatically fixed overhead. GMV/parcels is a ratio, not a proven order AOV.

133 policies were screened on 1,000 worlds; 14 finalists were evaluated on 10,000 fresh matched worlds. The default conditional software candidate is `P_SOFTWARE_70_88`: a maximum internal ceiling of 70%, planning utilization 88%. It is not a promise of 70% realized internal share. Central year-5 internal share is 54.7162%; held-out average is approximately 53.6786%.

Central five-year project NPV is Rp0.572988151470tn, IRR 92.5543%, simple payback 1.39555 years. Initial software capex is Rp0.18tn, working capital Rp0.0018tn, year-1 transition Rp0.06tn, and year-5 software refresh Rp0.09tn.

On 10,000 held-out worlds, software 70/88 mean NPV is Rp0.509018511554tn, p10 Rp−0.160507609859tn, positive-NPV fraction 80.49%, and service-violation-world fraction 1.79%. These describe the authored distributions. Existing-TMS rules 70/88 is a close challenger with mean NPV about Rp0.46853tn; software wins 52.4% of matched worlds. Large physical expansion loses value under central assumptions. The higher-return software 75/100 policy has materially worse service risk.

All 133 evaluated policies fail strict positive annual group operating-profit growth in at least one central year under flat commercial demand/monetization, 2.5% logistics inflation and zero other net contribution change. Default central software group OP is `[4.57557157625012,4.2550704607093035,3.7802521560976974,3.250883460000141,2.7195305465001467]` Rp tn. A constant annual increase in separate non-logistics net contribution must exceed about Rp0.531353913tn/year to close every annual-growth gap. This is a required threshold, not a proved benefit.

Present the product confidently while preserving these results. Do not turn a positive project NPV into an annual group-profit-growth pass, investment approval, empirical customer retention, fee relief or measured savings.

## Geographic and time-profile interpretation

Regional scope assumes 400m annual parcels, or 20% of national volume, divided over 365 days. Nine selected corridor markets use 80% population proxy and 20% authored activity. This is a planning allocation, not observed parcel demand. The graph has 16 nodes, 17 corridors, 34 directed arcs, four hypothetical facility profiles and 36 lanes. Street access distances are not supplied as measured values.

Intraday rates use an authored shape normalized so trapezoidal integration over 07:00–19:00 equals the daily demand. Weekly multipliers average one. The shaded profile range is a scenario variation; it is not a trained forecasting confidence interval. National-city assignments are illustrative market-type mappings, not measured city demand.

## Current presentation and review instructions

# Presentation and review requirements

These user instructions apply to NexoraOps and future work on its deliverables.

## Audience and voice

Present the final idea as an operating product: “If NexoraOps already existed, here is what it would look like.” Judges understand that it is a prototype. Do not fill the product with “Need validation,” “Further justification needed,” “Planned,” or equivalent drafting status. Keep material definitions and assumptions where they help the reader interpret the result. Do not imply live telemetry, measured savings, research findings, investment approval, or empirical forecast accuracy that does not exist.

Create a finished, presentation-ready deliverable for its intended audience. Adapt the language, tone, and structure to the task—business, academic, technical, or creative. Write naturally and precisely, with specific content rather than generic filler, inflated claims, or repetitive summaries.

Keep assistant-to-user commentary out of the file. Do not include conversational introductions, explanations of what was created, references to prompts or AI tools, offers of further help, or instructions addressed conversationally to the requester. Avoid “key takeaway” boxes, canned conclusions, decorative callouts, and unnecessary explanations. Include substantive analysis, methodology, definitions, and limitations when the reader needs them.

Use clean, restrained design: consistent typography, clear hierarchy, sensible spacing, aligned tables, and a limited palette suited to the project. Avoid checkerboard patterns, automatic alternating row fills, excessive borders, and decoration without a purpose. Follow supplied templates and brand guidelines, subject to explicit user preferences.

For XLSX, do not freeze rows or columns. Use readable dimensions, consistent units and number formats, functional formulas where appropriate, and purposeful formatting for inputs, headings and totals. For CSV, preserve a clean, consistent data structure without decorative rows or commentary. For DOCX and PDF, use coherent headings, readable tables, and deliberate pagination without clipped content or awkward breaks.

Use genuine, traceable sources. Cite external evidence appropriately and provide APA 7 references where applicable, using real bibliographic details and links or DOIs. Do not expose upload filenames, local paths, tool identifiers, or internal cell references as audience-facing citations. Identify supplied material by a meaningful document title or accurate description. Label estimates “Planning assumptions” or “Team assumptions,” as appropriate. Never invent attribution, research or approval.

Ask before material new assumptions affecting scope, conclusions, financial results or interpretation. Resolve routine wording and formatting independently. Current confirmed scope and recorded planning assumptions already have authorization; do not re-open them as unnecessary permission requests.

Before delivery, check calculations, citations, consistency and layout, and remove drafting residue. Keep the handoff brief and put necessary production notes outside audience-facing files.

## Review-and-revision method

1. Define success using required content, constraints, audience, references and standards. Resolve routine choices independently; clarify material new assumptions.
2. Produce a complete first attempt.
3. Perform a distinct demanding review. Use an independent critic when available; claim independent review only when it occurred. Compare the actual output with requirements and references.
4. Score applicable dimensions from 0–10: task fulfillment, correctness, completeness, clarity/usability, and presentation/execution. A 5 needs substantial revision, 7 is usable with clear weaknesses, 8.5 is strong with minor issues, and 9 needs exceptional supporting evidence. A 10 is extraordinary across every dimension. Justify judgments with observable strengths and defects.
5. Verify calculations, formulas, sources, behavior, layout and consistency where possible. Inspect actual output. Distinguish tested results from subjective judgments and unchecked claims.
6. Rank issues by impact. Correct critical errors and unmet requirements, then substantive weaknesses, then polish. Recheck affected behavior after revision.

Repeat for up to four substantive rounds. Stop when applicable dimensions reach at least 8.5 and no critical errors or explicit unmet requirements remain. Do not increase scores merely to pass, and do not continue without a concrete improvement. Deliver the strongest verified result, disclosing material unresolved limitations outside the audience-facing deliverable. Do not claim perfection or checks that did not occur. Keep ratings and critique exchanges out of deliverables unless requested.

The final user message contained a line-wrap splice in the last sentence of this instruction. The operational meaning retained here is “Never raise a score merely to pass or keep revising without a concrete improvement.”


## Current product and technical specification


### PRODUCT.md

# Product brief

## Intended experience

NexoraOps presents the proposed platform as an operating logistics product. A judge can inspect the network, change a decision, compare consequences, respond to disruption, and explain the investment result without reading implementation notes.

The product connects three practical questions: where to allocate parcels, how to preserve service when capacity changes, and whether the investment improves the group financial result. The default scenario is Greater Jakarta, and the default view is a navigable 3D regional twin on desktop.

## Navigation and responsibilities

| Group | Screen | Main job | Decision or interaction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Monitor | Ringkasan | Financial and operating summary | Read project return and annual group-profit result together |
| Monitor | Digital twin | Regional network and facility activity | Select hub, orbit camera, inspect capacity, change scale and layer |
| Monitor | Proyeksi | Intraday and seven-day workload | Compare time profiles with physical capacity |
| Putuskan | Policy Lab | Allocation and investment tradeoffs | Select a matrix cell and recalculate matched-world outcomes |
| Putuskan | Kapasitas & mitra | Physical capacity and planning limits | Compare facilities and national market utilization |
| Putuskan | Insiden & tindakan | Four-hour Cawang outage | Compare, apply and undo responses |
| Evaluasi | Dampak | Incremental project and group P&L | Change finance assumptions and inspect annual cash flows |
| Evaluasi | Tahapan penerapan | Operating sequence and investment criteria | Read phased operating actions and decision gates |
| Evaluasi | Bukti & asumsi | Evidence provenance | Inspect sources and assumptions; import a scenario |

## Shared state

Policy family, maximum internal ceiling, planning utilization limit, workload multiplier, available capacity, travel condition, cost inflation, discount rate, and non-logistics contribution carry across analytical views. The regional incident is a separately scoped four-hour event: applying it selects the incident's defined base policy, resets operating stress controls, and updates regional allocations. It does not silently annualize a single disruption into five-year savings.

The timeline controls the illustrative replay. Daily and annual metrics retain their full-period scope. Moving an actor represents aggregate activity; it does not represent a GPS-tracked vehicle or one physical parcel.

## Presentation language

Use direct operating language: “Jaringan pengiriman,” “Bandingkan respons,” “Terapkan skenario,” and “Dampak keuangan.” Avoid assistant commentary, work-in-progress badges, generic sales filler, and review residue. One discreet prototype/data indicator is sufficient. Relevant assumptions belong beside the affected metric or in evidence details.

Financial results remain exact even when unfavorable. A presentation-ready product can show that a policy has a positive project NPV while the wider group-profit constraint does not pass. It cannot describe an unpassed constraint as a successful outcome.

## Boundaries

This deliverable is an offline presentation prototype with functional local calculations. It provides no live company connection, account system, operational dispatch integration, production authorization, trained forecasting service, or street-level geospatial inventory. These technical boundaries appear in handoff documentation, rather than as repeated drafting warnings in the interface.


### DESIGN.md

# NexoraOps design system

## Visual direction

A white, spacious operations platform with restrained burnt orange. The primary visual occupies most of each page: a twin, a large time-series chart, a decision matrix, or a financial comparison. Details follow selection or appear below the main result. Vertical scrolling is deliberate.

Lintara informs the large scene, slim metrics strip, replay controls and clean business summaries. JakCool informs the app shell, grouped navigation, chart priority and contextual inspector. The warehouse reference informs the cutaway's open roof, racks, pallets, conveyors, docks and small animated vehicles. NexoraOps uses its own identity and logistics content.

## Tokens

| Role | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | `#FFFFFF` |
| Workspace | `#F6F7F9` |
| Primary | `#C65317` |
| Hover | `#A94010` |
| Selected surface | `#FFF0E6` |
| Main text | `#202833` |
| Supporting text | `#637080` |
| Border | `#E3E7EC` |
| Positive operating result | Muted forest green |
| Negative result | Muted rust |

Use system sans-serif fonts, avoiding runtime font requests. Body text is about 15px, page headings about 29px, section headings 17–19px, and main metric values 27–32px. Small captions remain secondary; they do not carry the central argument.

## Layout

The desktop sidebar is 224px wide. The top bar is 76px high. Main content has 24–32px spacing. Use no more than two major columns, with a 272px contextual inspector beside the scene. The scene height is 525px on ordinary desktop and 620px on large screens. Tables have generous row heights, consistent number alignment and quiet dividers.

At narrower widths, major columns stack. On phones, the navigation becomes a drawer, metrics use two columns, and the initial network view is 2D. Tables retain their column widths inside a horizontal scrolling container. A user can still inspect facilities and run calculations.

## Motion and rendering

Use orthographic camera projection, soft colors and diffuse directional lighting. Roads follow schematic corridor geometry; buildings remain procedural. Trucks and parcels are small relative to buildings. Actor count follows regional demand and selected-facility activity, with explicit aggregation. Canvas fallback uses the same camera and geometry when WebGL2 cannot be created.

Respect reduced-motion preferences by starting replay paused. Keep camera controls, pause, speed and timeline accessible independently of drag gestures. Low-quality mode reduces decorative building count, leaving numerical results unchanged.

## Copy and evidence

The app describes operating actions and consequences. It does not include “planned,” “needs validation,” “further justification needed,” reviewer scores, prompts, AI-tool descriptions, or offers of help. Team assumptions remain identified where they affect interpretation. Evidence citations use meaningful source titles, not upload paths or internal tool identifiers.


### docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

# Architecture

## Runtime

The application is a static ES-module website. It uses browser APIs, authored SVG charts, native HTML controls, local storage, a module worker and a procedural 3D renderer. No build-time or runtime package installation is required.

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `app.js` | Shared state, nine views, controls, regional allocation, import/export and replay |
| `engine.js` | Float64 national operating model, investment finance, statistics and transport solver |
| `worker.js` | Asynchronous matched-world simulation and heatmap recalculation |
| `scene.js` | Procedural geometry, orthographic camera, picking labels, aggregate animation, WebGL2 and Canvas fallback |
| `styles.css` | Layout, tokens, responsive behavior, print and reduced-motion styling |
| `data/` | Model configuration, named worlds, reference outcomes, regional fixtures and evidence |

## Calculation pipeline

A policy sets an internal-share ceiling and utilization limit. The engine evaluates the chosen operating conditions and a current-policy counterfactual using the same demand, traffic and cost conditions. Incremental project cash flows are then calculated. A separate group-profit bridge evaluates each annual growth step.

The regional solver uses nine demand zones, shared hub capacities and finite carrier reservation capacity. It solves a continuous transport allocation, not a vehicle-routing problem. Precomputed default regional fixtures preserve the original Python results. Custom settings trigger a browser solve. Current-policy custom scenarios preserve the baseline 50% internal allocation per zone when capacity permits; displaced internal volume becomes deferred demand.

The website fetches compact reference JSON on startup. The 10,000 named-world file is fetched only when a worker calculation begins. Simulation progress is posted in batches. Parameter signatures prevent a completed old result from appearing as the result for newly selected controls.

## Data contracts

Volumes in the national engine are billions of parcels per year. Money is Rp trillions. Regional volumes are individual parcels per day or per four-hour window; regional money is IDR. Conversion to display format happens at the view boundary.

Scenario JSON uses `schema_version: 1.0.0`. Import limits file size to 1MB, accepts known policy IDs, allowlists enum controls and bounds numeric controls. An export includes the state, active policy, annual results, scope and matching Monte Carlo summary if available. CSV uses a single header row and consistent annual-national units.

## Persistence

Device storage holds one active scenario. It does not upload data. JSON provides portable restoration. Results are reproducible because the exported worlds retain their sampled values and identity; the browser does not attempt to reproduce NumPy PCG64 with a different random-number generator.

## Renderer

WebGL2 uses instanced cube geometry and a faceted tree mesh with a simple lighting shader. The fallback projects the same 3D boxes through the camera matrix and paints visible faces to Canvas 2D. Decorative quality is reduced for the fallback. No downloaded models or textures are required.

Selection is exposed through DOM buttons, so a hub can be chosen without pixel-perfect canvas picking. National cities and 2D hubs support keyboard activation. The parameter drawer and guided tour keep keyboard focus inside their active dialog.

## Hosting

`npm run build` copies the website into `dist/`. This is a static build; no server rendering or edge runtime is used. Vercel can serve all assets directly. Worker and JSON paths remain same-origin. A static host must serve JavaScript with a JavaScript content type.


### docs/MODEL_AND_SIMULATION.md

# Model and simulation specification

## Scope and accounting

Case anchors: 2 billion annual parcels, 50% internal delivery, Rp8,000 average internal cost, Rp12,000 external cost, and Rp5 trillion 2025 group operating profit. The implied delivery spend is Rp20 trillion. The full group P&L is not identified by these facts. The default other net operating contribution change is zero; it is a planning assumption.

The four national market types are dense urban, suburban, regional, and difficult/inter-island. Their planning weights are 35%, 30%, 25%, and 10%. These weights do not claim observed Nexora demand shares. Annual commercial demand and monetization remain flat in the central finance case. Changing parcel workload changes logistics workload for both policy and counterfactual; it does not automatically create revenue or customer retention benefits.

## National allocation

For every world and year, the engine computes demand, cost inflation, traffic-sensitive variable cost, available internal capacity and external capacity. Non-current policies rank 24 marginal tranches in each of four types, creating 96 stable-ranked opportunities. It accepts economically beneficial tranches up to the selected ceiling, then applies the package ramp and adoption level. The ceiling can remain inactive when additional insourcing has no economic value.

The model retains committed fixed costs. Internal overtime and route-mix costs rise nonlinearly. External reservations are finite. Unserved demand is retained and charged emergency/deferred handling; it does not disappear from parcel conservation.

Planning service is a modeled feasibility measure using annual shortfall, daily surge overload and high-utilization lateness. A world violates the service condition if any year has more than 0.5% annual unserved demand or less than 95% planning service. This is not an observed on-time-delivery rate.

## Investment finance

Cash flow includes initial capex, working capital, transition expense, recurring software and maintenance costs, tax on positive EBIT, depreciation, software refresh in year 5, vehicle replacement in year 6 where relevant, working-capital release and conservative physical salvage.

The default horizon is five years; archived analysis also tests three and seven. The nominal IDR discount rate is 14%, with 11–18% sensitivity. The website calculates NPV, IRR, simple and discounted payback, peak funding and the group operating-profit bridge.

A positive NPV is incremental project value against the same-world counterfactual. It does not imply that total group profit rises in every year. Under the central flat-commercial, 2.5% logistics-inflation, zero-other-contribution assumptions, 0 of the 133 evaluated policies pass the strict annual group-profit-growth condition.

## Reproducible simulation

The archived study screens 133 policies on 1,000 worlds, then evaluates 14 finalists on 10,000 fresh worlds. It includes 66 heatmap cells, stress tests, structural alternatives, matched policy comparisons and a regional incident. Screening seed: 20261027. Holdout seed: 20261101.

The website stores the 10,000 held-out named worlds as JSON. A 200- or 1,000-world browser run uses the first corresponding subset; a 10,000-world run reproduces the full holdout. Each policy receives the same named worlds, avoiding noisy comparisons between unrelated draws.

The archived heatmap uses 1,000 worlds per cell for software at 88% utilization. Browser recalculation uses 100 worlds per cell to keep all 66 cells interactive. The active label distinguishes the reference matrix from the browser result. A cell with an internal ceiling above the economic realization is marked as an inactive ceiling, rather than a hard constraint failure. Service-risk flags remain separate in the interpretation.

Curated stresses include campaign workload, capacity loss, slower travel, weak software productivity/adoption, and implementation overrun. The browser worker applies the same stress transformations as the central view. Custom sliders remain within bounded ranges.

## Regional allocation and geography

The selected Greater Jakarta market assumes 400 million annual parcels, divided by 365 to give approximately 1.096 million parcels/day. Nine zone weights combine 80% population proxy and 20% authored activity. This allocation is not measured parcel demand.

The corridor model contains 16 nodes, 17 corridors, 34 directed arcs, four hypothetical facility profiles and 36 candidate lanes. Distances use a weighted shortest-path corridor graph. Straight drawn lines and square zones are schematic; they are not street routes or cadastral catchments.

The regional continuous transport solver minimizes internal route cost, external carrier cost, emergency capacity and deferred handling. Hub capacities are shared across zones. The current policy holds 50% internal allocation per zone when capacity permits. Targeted packages raise existing capacity by 18%; large expansion activates the Bekasi candidate and multiplies physical capacity by 1.35. Package cost modifiers, handling rates, local productivity and SLA travel limits are team assumptions.

No detailed OSM, Overture, building or settlement extract is included as downloaded measured data. The procedural scene illustrates the operational concept. Regional savings are not multiplied uniformly across Indonesia.

## Incident

Cawang loses 50% of its capacity for four hours of a twelve-hour operating day. This is a 16.67% effective daily loss at that hub: 240,000 becomes 200,000 daily available capacity. The defined incident uses the rules 70/88 policy. The app compares fixed-route deferral, reallocation within existing hubs and reservations, and emergency 3PL capacity.

The four-hour response is combined with the unchanged other eight hours. Daily committed cost is counted once. Deferred volume remains visible. Applying an incident response affects regional operations, while annual project cash flows remain on their explicitly chosen annual scenario.

## Time profiles

Intraday rates use an authored seven-point shape normalized so trapezoidal integration across 07:00–19:00 equals daily regional demand. Weekly multipliers are normalized to an average of one, so a seven-day view sums to seven daily equivalents. The displayed band is a scenario variation around this profile. It is not a trained forecast confidence interval or a measured forecast accuracy claim.

## Reference outcome

For software 70/88: central NPV Rp0.572988151470 trillion; IRR 92.5543%; payback 1.39555 years. Holdout mean NPV Rp0.509018511554 trillion, p10 Rp−0.160507609859 trillion, positive fraction 80.49%, service-violation world fraction 1.79%. Realized internal share differs between the central case (54.7162% in year 5) and the held-out average (53.6786%).

Central annual group profit is approximately Rp4.576T, Rp4.255T, Rp3.780T, Rp3.251T and Rp2.720T. A separate constant annual increase in other net operating contribution must exceed approximately Rp0.531354T/year to close every annual-growth gap. This is a threshold requirement, not a credited benefit.


### docs/DEPLOYMENT.md

# Deployment and operation

## Vercel project

1. Extract the ZIP into a working folder. The application root is `NexoraOps/`, containing `package.json`, `vercel.json`, `website/`, and `dist/`.
2. Run `npm test` and `npm run build` from that root with Node.js 20 or later.
3. Add the folder to a repository or import it into a Vercel project. Select **Other** if a framework preset is requested.
4. Set root directory to the folder containing `package.json`, build command to `npm run build`, and output directory to `dist`.
5. No install command is needed beyond the host's standard package handling; the dependency list is empty. No environment variables are required.
6. Build the deployment, then inspect the host's preview URL. Confirm the nine navigation screens, JSON loading, worker progress, JSON/CSV downloads and facility selection before presenting.

Only `dist/` is published. The casebook, analytical workbook and historical discussion remain outside the public website unless explicitly added to a hosting output folder.

## Static hosting alternative

Any static host can serve `dist/`. All runtime assets are relative and same-origin. Requests for `.js` need a JavaScript MIME type, JSON and GeoJSON need readable responses, and module workers need ordinary same-origin script access. A `file://` launch is unsuitable.

## Session behavior

The app opens in Digital twin. On phones it starts with the 2D map. If a scenario was saved on the device, bounded settings restore; the replay state starts according to reduced-motion preference. **Kembali ke asumsi sentral** in the parameter drawer restores the default 70/88 software scenario.

A 10,000-world run loads approximately 7.7MB of JSON once per worker lifecycle. Monte Carlo runs in the background. The worker can be canceled. A device's calculation and rendering performance depend on its browser and hardware; no universal 60fps guarantee is made.

## Presentation sequence

Use Digital twin → facility cutaway → Proyeksi → Policy Lab → Insiden & tindakan → Dampak. Keep the optional tour available for a self-guided judge. The default software recommendation balances downside and service risk; a higher-return 100% utilization policy illustrates the cost of removing capacity headroom.

The finance view should show both project returns and the annual group-profit test. The product narrative is selective allocation and resilient coordination, with investment evaluated against a rules-only alternative.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Data load error | Serve through HTTP; verify JSON files are present in `dist/data/` |
| Worker error | Verify `worker.js`, `engine.js`, and `worlds.json` have same-origin URLs and correct MIME types |
| Blank or slow hardware 3D | The renderer automatically uses Canvas projection if WebGL2 is unavailable; 2D remains selectable |
| Heavy scene | Choose **Ringan** in display quality; pause replay for a static view |
| Saved settings seem unexpected | Reset to central assumptions, then save again |
| Import fails | Use an exported version 1.0.0 scenario under 1MB with a recognized policy |
| Local storage unavailable | Use JSON export/import for portable state |

No production dispatch action, payment, external message or operational control is triggered by any button.

The current design feels cramped, fragmented, and overloaded. Redesign its layout and visual hierarchy substantially. Preserve the logistics functionality, but distribute information more thoughtfully across pages, tabs, and contextual panels.

DESIGN DIRECTION

Create a spacious, light, calm operations platform with readable typography, large analytical visuals, and clear priorities.

Follow JakCool for the application shell, sidebar, page headings, chart layouts, and supporting panels. Follow Lintara for the immersive digital twin, compact metrics strip, and timeline controls. Adapt these patterns to Nexora’s logistics domain without copying their branding or station-specific content.

LAYOUT AND DENSITY

Design at a realistic desktop viewport of 1440 × 900. Keep text readable at normal zoom.

Use a collapsible sidebar around 224–240 px wide, a restrained top bar, and generous content margins.

Give each page one dominant visual: a map, 3D twin, forecast chart, heatmap, or financial comparison.

Use a maximum of two main content columns. Supporting panels should remain clearly secondary.

Show only three or four essential headline metrics.

Use 24–32 px spacing between major sections and comfortable padding within panels.

Allow vertical scrolling. Do not shrink content to fit every detail into the first viewport.

Reveal detailed information through selection, tabs, expandable sections, and drawers.

Avoid nested cards, excessive borders, permanent warning boxes, and rows of tiny widgets.

TYPOGRAPHY AND COLOUR

Use a clean sans-serif with approximately 16 px body text, 14 px supporting labels, and 28–32 px page titles. Avoid tiny uppercase technical labels and excessive monospace text.

Use a very light grey background, white surfaces, dark slate text, subtle borders, and a restrained teal or blue accent. Reserve orange and red for actionable warnings. Use colour consistently across maps and charts.

NAVIGATION

Support these connected pages:
Overview; Digital Twin; Forecasts; Policy Lab; Capacity & Partners; Incidents & Actions; Impact; Rollout.

Place Evidence & Assumptions in a secondary navigation position. Group the main navigation under Monitor, Decide, and Evaluate.

PAGE COMPOSITION

Digital Twin:
Make the geographic network or 3D scene occupy most of the workspace. Place a slim metrics strip above it and playback/timeline controls below. Open hub or lane details when an object is selected. Keep detailed scenario settings behind a clearly labelled control.

Forecasts:
Use a large chart with a clear forecast boundary and uncertainty band. Add a smaller supporting panel explaining demand drivers and capacity risks. Put secondary charts further down the page. Provide simple time-horizon controls.

Policy Lab:
Give the heatmap enough room to read comfortably. Use colour to communicate the overall pattern, with detailed values shown on hover or selection. Keep only essential controls visible. Selecting a policy reveals its outcome distribution, service trade-offs, and an “Apply policy” action.

Incidents & Actions:
Use a readable incident list and a focused selected-incident workspace. Present the problem in plain language, then compare response options with clear cost, capacity, and service consequences.

Impact:
Start with a few prominent outcomes. Follow with a large operating-profit bridge and baseline-versus-proposed comparison. Place investment returns, cash flows, assumptions, and detailed tables below or in tabs.

INTERACTION AND COPY

Keep the selected scenario, geography, and comparison baseline consistent across pages. Use plain labels such as “Delivery cost per parcel,” “Capacity shortfall,” and “Compare responses.”

Include a discreet “Prototype · simulated data” indicator. Treat all example numbers as illustrative. Do not invent live integrations, measured forecast accuracy, or validated savings.

Generate the Digital Twin, Forecasts, Policy Lab, and Impact screens first, using one consistent design system. Prioritise a clear first glance: the user should immediately understand the page’s purpose, main result, and next action.

Judge the result by readability and hierarchy, not by how much information fits on screen.

## Historical appendix B — completed analysis master, version 1

Stage-specific implementation and PDF-availability statements are historical. Numerical findings remain binding unless superseded by tested changes above.

# Nexora Master Context Pack

Version 1.0.0 · October 27, 2026

## Read first and current state

National analysis, financial modelling, policy search, simulation, stress, structural sensitivity, prototype data, workbook and reports are complete within documented access limits. **Detailed street/building geospatial acquisition remains PARTIAL.** The regional package is a labelled corridor fallback. No website was built or deployed.

No evaluated national rollout satisfies the strict central annual group-profit-growth gate. Do not describe positive project NPV as investment approval. Read `Nexora_Methodology_and_Findings.md`, then `Nexora_Prototype_Handoff.md`, `data/config.json` and `data/reference_fixtures.json`. The ZIP contains all companion data, code, draws and evidence. The original incoming brief is preserved unchanged once at the end of this pack.

## User steering and scope

The exact instruction was: **“Run this. Good luck”**. No subsequent user steering changed the brief. The user delegated remaining researched assumptions, not deployment or external communications. All confirmed choices in the original brief remain binding. No survey findings or completed interviews were supplied. Print-on-demand, retention, fee relief, subsidies and new commercial demand remain outside core benefits.

## Completed and outstanding

Completed: baseline reconciliation; primary-source research and access attempts; 133-policy screening; 14 fresh finalists; 66 numeric heatmap cells; nine stresses; eight structural variants; three-/five-/seven-year finance; regional nine-/18-zone/proxy LP comparisons; 200 switching worlds; a four-hour incident; JSON/GeoJSON, fixtures, code and workbook exports; analytical and workbook QA.

Outstanding: actual buffered street/building/settlement data, detailed access/turn restrictions, real lane/hub/fleet costs and capacities, implementation quotes, carrier reservations, empirical service calibration, survey/retention effects, supported group-profit forecasts, prototype implementation and TypeScript parity. Pilots and rollout stages are proposals, not completed actions.

## Decision register

**D001: Preserve settled choices and analysis-only scope.** User-authorised incoming brief. No website, deployment or communications. User-authorised.

**D002: Use an incremental group-profit bridge.** The case residual does not identify a full historical P&L. Zero other net contribution is disclosed, not a fixed-overhead fact. Analyst chosen under delegated authority.

**D003: Evaluate five years, test three/seven.** Software/vehicle commercial cycle; refresh, replacement and conservative residuals are explicit. Analyst chosen under delegated authority.

**D004: Use 14% nominal IDR discount, test 11–18%.** Authored premium above sourced sovereign benchmarks. Not observed Nexora WACC. Analyst chosen under delegated authority.

**D005: Separate national types from regional LP.** Do not multiply a Jakarta saving uniformly across national parcels. Analyst chosen under delegated authority.

**D006: Use a labelled corridor fallback.** Acquisition restricted. Full street/building validation remains PARTIAL; no invented observed features. Analyst chosen under delegated authority.

**D007: Retain an existing-TMS rules challenger.** Current operations already have routine technology. Software receives only incremental productivity and capacity benefits. Analyst chosen under delegated authority.

**D008: Identify a conditional software candidate.** Risk score plus no worse matched service. This is not rollout approval. Analyst chosen under delegated authority.

**D009: Reject unconditional national rollout.** Zero of 133 central policies pass every annual profit-growth test. Analyst chosen under delegated authority.

**D010: Export named draws for frontend parity.** Do not rely on cross-language PCG64 implementations. Keep float64 and stable tranche ties. Analyst chosen under delegated authority.

## Findings and investment interpretation

No national rollout clears all requirements in the central model. All **133 evaluated policies fail positive annual group operating-profit growth** in at least one year under flat commercial demand and monetisation, 2.5% nominal logistics cost inflation, and zero other net operating-profit change. Positive incremental project value does not override this constraint.

The best evaluated investment candidate under the stated service and downside preference is **P_SOFTWARE_70_88**. It uses software-led allocation with an 88% capacity buffer setting and a 70% maximum internal-share ceiling. Its realised internal share is only **53.7%** in held-out worlds. The ceiling is not a forecast of 70% insourcing.

Central initial spending is Rp180 billion of software/integration capex, Rp1.8 billion of working capital, and Rp60 billion of Year 1 transition expense. The five-year central NPV is **Rp0.573 trillion** at 14%, project IRR **92.6%**, payback **1.40 years**, and discounted payback **1.57 years**. The asymmetric overrun distribution raises expected initial capex to Rp204.4 billion.

Across 10,000 held-out worlds, mean NPV is **Rp0.509 trillion**, p10 NPV **Rp-0.161 trillion**, and **80.5%** of worlds have positive NPV. These describe the authored distributions, not empirical confidence about Nexora.

The existing-TMS rules package is a close challenger. The software candidate exceeds `P_RULES_70_88` by only Rp40.5 billion mean NPV and wins 52.4% of matched worlds. The paired p10 difference is Rp-253.7 billion. Urban-heavy weights favour rules, while regional-heavy weights make both lose. This supports validating the rules/configuration alternative before committing to software. No pilot has occurred.

The maximum expected-return alternative is `P_SOFTWARE_75_100`, with mean NPV Rp1.016 trillion. It has planning-service violations in 27.9% of worlds and fails the selected service safeguard. Large physical expansion loses value in the central model. Targeted capacity can become preferable under a higher fixed-cost decomposition or a flatter marginal route-mix gradient.

| Policy | Mean NPV, Rp tn | p10, Rp tn | Service-violation worlds | Year 1 incremental EBIT, Rp tn |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P_CURRENT | 0.000 | 0.000 | 6.9% | 0.000 |
| P_RULES_70_88 | 0.469 | -0.218 | 2.1% | 0.142 |
| P_SOFTWARE_70_88 | 0.509 | -0.161 | 1.8% | 0.062 |
| P_SOFTWARE_75_100 | 1.016 | 0.258 | 27.9% | 0.208 |
| P_TARGETED_75_100 | 0.359 | -0.348 | 6.1% | -0.030 |
| P_LARGE_85_100 | -3.220 | -4.119 | 0.6% | -0.620 |

Central annual candidate group OP: `[4.57557157625012, 4.2550704607093035, 3.7802521560976974, 3.250883460000141, 2.7195305465001467]` Rp tn. Matching current-policy group OP: `[4.5, 3.9875000000000007, 3.462187500000006, 2.923742187500011, 2.3718357421875105]`. Cash flows: `[-0.1818, 0.08144582947509302, 0.2537049593532561, 0.29309043175619925, 0.30017019255010147, 0.21675194736385622]` Rp tn, including time zero. Central project NPV: `0.572988151470` Rp tn; IRR `0.925542833098`; payback `1.395554627` years; discounted payback `1.565298506`; peak funding `0.181800000` Rp tn.

Annual-growth passes: **0/133**. Required constant annual increase in other net operating contribution: more than `0.531353913` Rp tn/year. This is a break-even requirement, not a supported benefit. Central break-even initial capex: `0.592778637` Rp tn under linked transition/refresh/tax treatment. No approved budget exists.

The model does not support Rp5,000–6,000 blended delivery costs. A regional-heavy national mix reverses software/rules value, while high committed fixed costs or a flat marginal route-mix gradient can favour targeted expansion. Preserve these unfavourable findings when continuing.

## Model specification

National units are billion parcels/year, IDR/parcel and Rp trillion. Four market weights are 35/30/25/10%; historical internal shares 80/60/16/0%. Weighted costs reproduce 50% internal share and Rp8,000/Rp12,000. Capacity is 0.64/0.43/0.13/0.02 billion, interpreted as the minimum of sorter, linehaul and courier ceilings. Upgrades must expand all three.

For each type, q0 = two billion × weight × historical share. Fixed cost is 25% of historical internal spending. The variable intercept equals average cost × (1 − fixed share), less historical overtime per parcel. Overtime and route-mix equations are in the findings and `model.py`. Allocation uses 24 tranches/type, 96 stable-ranked midpoint savings, positive avoidable savings only, a share ceiling, then adoption/ramp. Carrier capacity and explicit deferred handling are finite. Fixed costs remain committed.

Rules receive allocation benefits only. Software affects 65% of variable cost, with a central 3% component improvement and 2% capacity release. Physical capex and fixed/maintenance costs remain even if capacity is unused. No internal-transfer, subsidy or retention revenue is credited. Matching worlds keep demand and commercial economics identical between policy/counterfactual.

Group OP = 5 − (matched current logistics cost − 20) + elapsed year × other net OP increase + incremental policy EBIT. The default other-net term is zero; the residual is not assumed wholly fixed overhead. Demand-axis workload is distinct from random variation around each axis point.

Finance is nominal IDR, unlevered, annual time zero/end-year cash flow. Main horizon five years, alternatives three/seven. Discount 14% (11–18% tested); general CIT 22%; no immediate incremental loss credit. Lives: software four, vehicles five, sortation eight, leasehold ten. Half-year first/last depreciation; 50% software refresh in Year 5; vehicle replacement in Year 6 for longer evaluation. Working capital 1% software plus 2% physical, released at the horizon. Software salvage zero; physical salvage 35% of remaining physical book value. No perpetuity value or invented financing.

## Executed analysis record

Final national runtime: `15.357` seconds, excluding export and later QA. Pilot sizes: 250/500/1,000. Screening: 133 × 1,000 policy-worlds. Fresh shortlist: 14 × 10,000. Heatmap: 66 × 1,000. Structural sensitivity: eight × 14 × 2,000. Regional switching: 200. Nine central stress definitions are in `results/analysis.json`.

Seeds: 20261027 screening, 20261101 holdout, 73027 regional. NumPy PCG64; Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.17.0, Matplotlib 3.10.8. Full held-out named arrays and policy NPVs are compressed NPZ; 200 reference worlds are JSON. Draws are created outside policy loops. Recommended-candidate NPVs were independently re-executed across all 10,000 worlds and matched saved outcomes.

Persistent parameter uncertainty includes productivity, adoption, overrun, inflation and shared demand/cost factors. Annual operating noise includes travel, demand, input/carrier price, capacity and a separate daily surge. Exact distributions, coefficients, truncation and correlations are in `model.py` and the assumption register below. Demand/travel share a factor; input/carrier prices share another. Adaptive allocation assumes rates/traffic/capacity observable for planning; fixed-priority structural sensitivity was executed. Percentiles are not empirical causal confidence intervals.

The risk score is E[NPV] − 0.5 × (E[NPV] − p10), with 0/0.25/1 alternatives. Service thresholds are 99.5% served, 95% planning feasibility, at most 10% worlds with any annual violation, and no worsening of matched current mean feasibility or world-violation frequency. Annual profit growth remains a separate gate.

Do not extrapolate one Jakarta saving uniformly.

## 1. Instruction to the receiving assistant

You are the analytical workstream for an Indonesian e-commerce business competition project. **Carry out the research, calculations, geospatial preparation, policy evaluation, Monte Carlo analysis, and financial modelling described below. Deliver the actual files, including a complete master context pack.** Do not stop at a proposed methodology or a list of things the user should calculate.

Otherwise use this extract and accurately describe your source access; do not claim you personally inspected the PDF.

The user has authorised you to independently research and select remaining technical and financial assumptions. Do not ask the user to invent costs, discount rates, elasticities, capacities, or forecast inputs. Make educated, documented assumptions and test consequential alternatives. **This chat does the analysis. A different chat will build the prototype from your outputs. Do not build or deploy the website.**

## 2. Project and strategic context

Nexora is fictional. Indonesia is the case market. NexExpress is its internal logistics arm, operating alongside third-party logistics providers, called 3PLs. All monetary case figures are Indonesian rupiah (IDR/Rp).

Official case question:

> How can Nexora achieve sustainable profitable growth while strengthening its competitive position and mitigating seller and buyer attrition in Indonesia's increasingly competitive e-commerce market?

The wider team has three working goals: grow transaction value, monetise sustainably, and deliver efficiently and reliably. This workstream concerns the third goal and its financial consequences. Buyer surveys have been distributed, and seller interviews are being prepared. No survey results, completed interview findings, or validated demand elasticities are supplied here. Print-on-demand is a separate growth hypothesis; do not incorporate its revenue or demand into this logistics model.

The operational hypothesis is that better allocation between NexExpress and 3PLs, more effective use of existing capacity, and selective investments can improve consolidated economics without sacrificing service. The answer is not assumed to be more insourcing everywhere. A current-policy or smaller-investment alternative is allowed to win.

The competition prototype will demonstrate a delivery operations control room, a policy heatmap, and incident-response decisions. It will contain actual browser-side numerical calculations and potentially thousands of Monte Carlo runs, using case anchors, external evidence, and explicit hypothetical operating assumptions. It is not a live company digital twin.

The user wants an optimistic but rational opportunity assessment. Interpret optimism as pursuing plausible improvements and staged investment in favourable locations, not forcing favourable assumptions or a positive result. Present a central case, a justified upside, and meaningful downside cases.

## 3. Confirmed user decisions

These choices are settled. Do not ask them again.

1. **Investment life:** choose the evaluation horizon from the proposed assets' and systems' economic lives. Explain the choice and test alternative horizons. Do not keep extending the horizon until IRR passes.
2. **Objective:** prioritise consolidated group operating-profit improvement, with investment economics and service safeguards also reported. Use NPV to assess value across mutually exclusive investment alternatives; do not rank different-sized projects solely by IRR.
3. **Budget:** no approved investment ceiling or required payback period exists. Evaluate a range of investment packages and show efficient trade-offs and break-even spending. Do not invent an approved budget.
4. **Operating scope:** compare both software-led coordination/allocation and more capital-intensive physical expansion. Include software-only, targeted shifts/vehicles/upgrades, and larger physical investment alternatives where supportable.
5. **Profit constraint:** the recommended rollout must preserve positive annual consolidated group operating-profit growth from Year 1. This is stricter than merely remaining profitable. Test it explicitly; do not disguise a failure.
6. **Commercial scope:** isolate logistics economics first. Hold underlying transaction demand and monetisation constant between each policy and its matching counterfactual. Additional demand, fee relief, retention gains, and shipping subsidies belong in separate optional extensions, not the core benefit calculation.
7. **Geography:** use a national financial perspective through transparent representative delivery-market types, plus a more detailed real-geography-grounded Greater Jakarta model for the prototype.
8. **Risk preference:** favour strong expected performance with tolerable downside; also display the maximum-expected-return alternative and explain the trade-off.
9. **Assumptions:** independently research and choose all other technical and financial assumptions, with provenance and sensitivity testing.
10. **Prototype AI:** no live Jev integration is required. A later prototype may use rule-based or scripted incident assessment labelled as a demo. Do not make AI API calls a dependency of this analysis.

## 5. Accounting and interpretation boundaries

Use these checks before designing the model:

- Current blend: 0.5 × Rp8,000 + 0.5 × Rp12,000 = Rp10,000 per parcel.
- Assuming aligned cost and volume scopes, implied delivery spending is 2bn × Rp10,000 = Rp20tn, comprising Rp8tn internal and Rp12tn external. This is derived, not an audited logistics P&L.
- Rp600tn / 2bn = Rp300,000 **GMV per parcel**, not proven average order value.
- Rp60tn / 2bn = Rp30,000 platform revenue per parcel on an aggregate basis; not marginal contribution per new parcel.
- Rp60tn − Rp24tn marketing − Rp5tn operating profit = Rp31tn other operating costs including logistics.
- Subtracting the derived Rp20tn delivery cost leaves Rp11tn as a conditional residual. It is not verified fixed overhead, technology expense, or a directly observed cost bucket. Do not confidently forecast it as wholly fixed.
- For unchanged volume and constant unit costs, shifting 10 percentage points internally mechanically saves Rp0.8tn annually. This is a reference calculation, not a forecast after capacity investment or changed route mix.
- Every Rp1,000 per parcel at two billion parcels equals Rp2tn annually. Use this as a unit sanity check.
- Current average cost is not marginal cost. The current internal network may already serve easier or denser lanes.
- Nexora–NexExpress internal transfers do not create consolidated profit. Do not invent new external revenue from transfer pricing.
- Include technology and expansion costs once, and distinguish capital expenditure from depreciation and recurring expense.
- Do not double-count failed-delivery expense already included in a cost estimate.
- A seller departure is not proportional GMV loss. A five-percentage-point repeat-buyer change is not automatically parcel growth or churn.
- Buyer retention, seller retention, and parcel growth can refer to the same underlying transactions; do not add them as independent benefits.
- Lower logistics cost alone does not prove improved buyer/seller retention. Report those as strategic hypotheses unless supported by additional evidence.

A prior informal proposal targeted 65–85% internal delivery and Rp5,000–6,000 blended costs. **These are not approved constraints or validated targets.** Do not centre the analysis on achieving them. At 80% internal share and Rp12,000 external cost, a Rp6,000 blend requires Rp4,500 internal cost; a Rp5,000 blend requires Rp3,250. Let the model establish what is plausible.

## 6. Research and evidence protocol

For each input distinguish:

1. CASE FACT — from the extract, with page.
2. DERIVED — arithmetic from case or external observations, with formula.
3. EXTERNAL OBSERVATION — primary-source benchmark with geography, date, unit, scope, and URL.
4. ASSUMPTION — an authored input or distribution, with reasoning and alternatives.

Prefer original datasets, official statistics, operator disclosures, official tariffs, primary research, and tool documentation. Check source applicability rather than collecting large volumes of citations. A public courier tariff is not internal marginal cost. A foreign efficiency estimate is not a Nexora saving coefficient.

For important assumptions record low/central/high or distribution parameters, correlation logic, impact sensitivity, and confidence in provenance. Distinguish parameter uncertainty from random operating variability. Do not claim that Monte Carlo confidence under assumed distributions is empirical confidence about Nexora.

Record retrieval dates, dataset versions, licenses/attribution, failures, and data-quality limitations. Do not use unrelated or poorly matched data simply to increase the number of sources. Do not silently replace inaccessible data with invented observations.

### Required investigation

Inspect and selectively use https://github.com/opengeos/geoai-skills for actual geographic grounding. It is a Claude Code plugin built on the GeoAI Python library, not guaranteed to be a drop-in plugin in your environment. Inspect current instructions and dependencies before use. If its launcher is unavailable, use compatible underlying Python/library or direct-data workflows, recording the route actually used. Do not claim the plugin executed if you merely followed its methods.

Relevant repository capabilities identified during planning include geographic inspection, Overture data extraction, raster processing, STAC imagery search, and imagery-based object detection. Overture workflows can retrieve buildings, places, transportation segments, and connectors. Primary transportation reference: https://docs.overturemaps.org/guides/transportation/ . Verify current coverage and schemas yourself.

Use existing mapped features first. Do not make satellite object detection mandatory when roads/buildings are already available. Some imagery workflows are US-specific, so check Indonesian coverage before choosing one. Additional sources such as OpenStreetMap, Indonesian official statistics, or gridded population products may be used where relevant and accessible; investigate rather than assume availability or completeness.

### Geographic analysis tasks

- Select and document a bounded Greater Jakarta study area: Jakarta, Bogor, Depok, Tangerang, Bekasi as appropriate to available data and feasible scope.
- Retrieve real geographic features and inspect coordinate systems, geometries, completeness, dates, and attributes.
- Construct a connected road-network representation with an appropriate buffer beyond the study boundary. Handle direction/access restrictions where available, disconnected components, and unreachable destinations explicitly.
- Use network travel distances for hub-to-zone accessibility. Label travel times as estimates unless sourced from actual measured times. Speed limits are not observed speeds; congestion needs separate assumptions or evidence.
- Select a manageable zoning resolution based on the analysis. Compare at least one alternative zoning or demand-distribution assumption to avoid false precision.
- Create transparent synthetic parcel-demand allocations using suitable settlement/population/building/activity proxies. These are not measured Nexora order locations. Normalise the chosen regional volume explicitly and vary proxy weights.
- Place **hypothetical** existing and candidate facilities at plausible accessible locations. Actual warehouse geometry does not establish NexExpress ownership or spare capacity.
- Calculate catchments, hub-to-zone distance/time matrices, service feasibility, and spatial cost drivers.
- Export an actual geographic decision layer: preferred delivery mode under each selected policy, marginal cost advantage, capacity pressure, and uncertainty/switching where supportable.

Use suitable geospatial tools as needed; you need not use deep learning to justify the work. Avoid arbitrary straight lines across barriers in the analytical routing network. Simplified lines may be used for visual overview only if the underlying distances are network-derived and the distinction is clear.

### National versus regional treatment

The case's two billion parcels are national annual volume. The Greater Jakarta volume is an assumption requiring a documented allocation method; do not treat all national parcels as local or reuse an arbitrary demonstration volume as observed data.

Use representative national delivery-market types with explicit weights and assumptions, such as dense urban, suburban/periurban, lower-density regional, and difficult/inter-island service where relevant. Weights must reconcile with national volume and baseline allocation/cost anchors. Test alternative weights. Do not multiply one Jakarta cost saving uniformly across the entire country. Label extrapolated results as modelled national scenarios.

## 8. Required analysis 1 — Baseline economics

Reconcile the baseline case, cost scopes, units, national annual and regional daily scales. Build a matching counterfactual for each forecast period. Keep demand and monetisation identical between policy and counterfactual in the core analysis; shared background inflation or exogenous changes may be modelled symmetrically and disclosed.

Use an incremental bridge from reported group operating profit where the case lacks a reliable full cost breakdown. Do not manufacture a fully identified historical P&L.

Baseline calibration should reproduce the 50% internal share and aggregate Rp8,000/Rp12,000 costs. A single calibration match does not identify fixed/variable splits or unique cost curves. Document alternative plausible decompositions and test their consequences.

Output baseline ledger, provenance, formulas, residual treatment, and assumptions.

## 9. Required analysis 2 — Marginal cost and capacity

Construct an explicit, operationally interpretable cost function:

- Existing committed capacity and utilisation.
- Avoidable/incremental labour, distance, vehicle time, fuel, handling, dispatch, and redelivery costs.
- Cost spreading as utilisation increases, where justified.
- Overtime, queues, missed cut-offs, and overflow near capacity.
- Discrete added shifts, vehicles, sorting upgrades, facilities, or collection points where applicable.
- Implementation delays, ramp-up, spare capacity, replacement expenditure, and stranded costs.
- External carrier tariffs, capacity, service availability, and possible repricing/contract effects.

Identify where the next increment of internal allocation is attractive relative to the actual alternative. Ensure spillovers between zones and shared hub capacity are respected; individually cheap zones may not all be simultaneously feasible.

Deliver marginal and average cost curves, capacity thresholds, expansion steps, and a geographic map of cost advantage. Do not hard-code a U-shaped curve or an interior optimum just to make 100% internal look bad. Any internal share can win if supported by the defined conditions.

## 10. Required analysis 3 — Policy and investment comparison

Distinguish decision variables from uncertain world conditions.

Decisions may include lane/zone allocation, overflow rules, dispatch/consolidation, added shifts, vehicles, hub upgrades, and phased investment. Uncertainties may include demand, travel time, cost inflation, productivity, failures, and implementation outcomes.

At minimum compare:

- Current 50/50 aggregate allocation, respecting its assumed geography.
- Simple feasible allocation/overflow rules.
- Software-led coordination/allocation with existing assets.
- Targeted capacity upgrades.
- More capital-intensive expansion.
- A capacity-aware recommended policy and a highest-expected-return alternative if different.

Evaluate no-investment alternatives fairly, including their costs and limitations. Do not award an intervention savings for capabilities implicitly assumed absent without explanation.

A grid or other transparent search is acceptable. Use a suitable solver if warranted. Report the best **evaluated** feasible policy unless global optimality is established. Target internal share and feasible realised internal share are different fields; unused capacity, unserved demand, and outsourced overflow must be visible.

Create:

1. A numeric heatmap with internal-share policies versus demand conditions, with expected incremental contribution and infeasible cells.
2. A companion geographic allocation/cost-advantage layer.
3. A policy comparison table including service and investment.

For each heatmap point compare against the counterfactual under the same demand level. Define the demand axis separately from stochastic demand variation around that level. Do not subtract a fixed 2025 profit from every higher-demand scenario and call all volume benefit policy benefit.

## 11. Required analysis 4 — Monte Carlo, stress, and sensitivity

Actually execute the numerical analysis, with recorded seeds, code, run counts, and runtime. Use seeded stochastic sampling so results are reproducible and policies encounter matched operating worlds. Preserve independent random-variable identities where possible when policy structures differ.

Start with a pilot performance/convergence check. A suggested plan is approximately 100 policy candidates × 1,000 sampled worlds for screening, then approximately 10,000 fresh worlds for shortlisted policies. Adjust to computational feasibility and convergence; these are planning sizes, not achieved results or mandatory wasteful counts. Do not claim a completed 10,000-run surface if only finalists received that many runs.

Document distributions, plausible correlations, constraints, and truncation. Include structural sensitivity to cost-curve forms, geographic allocation, demand proxies, and national weights, not just random noise around one preferred model.

Report expected/median outcomes, downside percentiles, share of runs improving over baseline, service violations, investment exposure, and policy-ranking stability. If you use a risk penalty or service threshold, specify and justify it and test alternatives. A 10th percentile outcome is not a 90% confidence interval for a real-world causal effect.

Stress at least: campaign surge, reduced hub capacity, corridor/travel-time disruption, weak productivity improvement, higher implementation costs, and external-carrier repricing. Include cases where the intervention is neutral or loses. Evaluate shortlisted policies on fresh draws rather than reporting only selection-sample winners.

Provide a sensitivity/tornado exhibit and break-even thresholds: which assumptions would reverse the recommendation, or cause it to miss profit/service requirements?

## 12. Required analysis 5 — Financial and service impact

### Profit and cash flow

Build a transparent consolidated operating-profit bridge and separate incremental investment cash-flow model. Account for technology implementation, recurring software/cloud/AI costs where relevant, integration, training, labour changes, transition costs, depreciation, maintenance, replacement, working capital, and taxes using researched or disclosed assumptions.

Use unlevered incremental project cash flows as the default; do not invent financing arrangements or present project IRR as equity IRR. Match nominal/real and currency treatment between cash flows and discount rates. Research a defensible nominal IDR discount-rate range; do not label an assumed hurdle rate as Nexora's observed WACC.

Choose the horizon from economic lives and rollout timing. Avoid a perpetuity terminal value in the main case. Use supported residual/salvage values, replacement, and decommissioning where relevant; expose any terminal-value dependence separately.

Calculate NPV, project IRR/XIRR as appropriate, payback, discounted payback, peak funding need, and break-even investment. For no-investment policies, IRR may be undefined; report N/A rather than fabricate it. If cash-flow sign changes produce multiple or unreliable IRRs, emphasise NPV and explain the issue. Do not silently turn operating profit into cash flow.

The user's desired hurdle is **IRR above the chosen discount rate**, with positive NPV over a justified horizon. This is an evaluation criterion, not permission to manufacture success. If it cannot be met, report that and investigate a smaller or differently phased policy within plausible assumptions.

### Annual growth constraint

Starting from reported 2025 group operating profit of Rp5tn, report annual group operating profit, year-on-year growth, the corresponding counterfactual, and incremental policy impact. Explicitly test positive annual profit growth from Year 1 and through the modelled horizon. Merely being above Rp5tn every year is insufficient if a later year declines.

Do not force the counterfactual or savings trajectory to make this pass. If no supported policy satisfies the user's constraint and investment criteria, state so and show the binding conditions and nearest feasible alternatives.

### Service safeguards

Define a manageable set of modelled measures: on-time performance or service feasibility, overflow/unserved parcels, backlog, and capacity utilisation. Justify thresholds, and distinguish daily planning feasibility from an empirically calibrated delivery probability. Cheap but infeasible policies must not win.

Do not claim a modelled service improvement has demonstrated a buyer-repeat or seller-retention effect. A concise strategic interpretation is welcome, but leave unmeasured benefits unquantified.

### Optional extensions

Only after completing core logistics analysis, optionally show separately budgeted subsidy reinvestment or commercial growth scenarios. Require incremental contribution to cover incentives, additional fulfilment, and related costs. No survey-derived elasticity is available in this brief. Keep these extensions out of headline core savings.

Explain data access, geography, accounting, assumptions, policy search, uncertainty, validation, findings, limitations, and recommended rollout. Include APA-style external references with URLs and dates. State what was actually executed versus only proposed.

### G. `Nexora_Master_Context_Pack.md`

This is a mandatory additional deliverable. The user explicitly wants to preserve the new chat's important context so another assistant can continue without the conversation history. It is a continuity record, not just an executive summary.

**Create it early and update it at major milestones**, after substantive decisions, after corrections or changes in scope, and before context compaction when feasible. Produce a final version after all outputs and validation results are known. Do not rely on remembering the whole session at the end. Maintain this file through the available persistent artifact/file workflow; keep reproducible working checkpoints where appropriate.

The final pack must contain:

1. **Read first and current state:** purpose, latest status, completed work, outstanding work, and a navigation guide. Distinguish verified execution, assumptions, proposed future work, and failed or blocked work.
2. **Original incoming context:** preserve this entire handoff document in a clearly delimited appendix, unchanged, including the confirmed user choices and case extract. A reference to a file that may not be available in a later chat is not sufficient. Avoid recursive copies of earlier pack versions; keep the initial brief once and a versioned change log.
3. **User steering and scope changes:** important subsequent user instructions, preferences, constraints, and authorisations, with exact wording where needed for meaning. Clearly identify changes that supersede the incoming brief.
4. **Decision register:** stable IDs, what was chosen, rationale, alternatives considered, reasons for rejecting or deferring them, evidence relied on, and whether the user approved the decision or the analyst chose it under delegated authority.
5. **Assumption register:** final values, ranges/distributions, units, provenance category, reasoning, correlations, revisions, sensitivity, and remaining uncertainty. Include evaluation life, discount rate, financial treatment, economic/physical life distinctions, geographic weights, demand proxies, costs, capacity, and service thresholds.
6. **Source and geography record:** exact source URLs, retrieval dates, dataset/repository versions or commit IDs where available, geographic scope, coordinate systems, coverage gaps, licenses, and actual access routes. Do not describe a catalogued dataset as downloaded or inspected unless it was.
7. **Model specification:** accounting boundaries, counterfactuals, equations, cost-curve forms, allocation rules, investments, rollout, demand normalisation, national extrapolation, cash-flow construction, risk objectives, and constraints. Preserve consequential implementation details needed to reproduce the results.
8. **Executed analysis record:** actual candidate counts, sampled-world counts, seeds, held-out evaluation design, distribution parameters, scenario definitions, software/dependency versions, runtime where measured, validation results, and outputs. Distinguish plans from achieved work.
9. **Findings and interpretation:** the recommended policy, alternatives, financial and service effects, break-even points, downside cases, structural sensitivities, and boundaries of what the evidence supports. Preserve failed or unfavourable results relevant to the recommendation.
10. **Corrections and abandoned approaches:** what was wrong or changed, why, and which former figures or conclusions must no longer be used. Label historical entries as superseded rather than leaving contradictory figures unresolved.
11. **Output manifest:** exact final filenames, available artifact IDs/links, schema versions, paths, checksums where practical, and what each file contains. Include the workbook, spatial outputs, JSON, code, findings, and prototype handoff. Do not invent identifiers or depend on temporary execution paths as the only locator.
12. **Prototype continuation:** which outputs drive each of the three screens, shared state and units, reference fixtures, simulated versus observed fields, known performance limitations, and remaining UI decisions.
13. **Open issues and next actions:** unresolved analytical questions, dependencies, limits, and a copy-ready continuation prompt for the prototype-building chat. The next assistant should not need to ask the user to repeat settled decisions.

Use a concise current-state section plus detailed appendices. The pack must be self-contained for understanding the work, while clearly identifying companion data/code files required to rerun it; it need not duplicate every raw geospatial feature or Monte Carlo draw. Do not replace specifics with statements such as “see earlier conversation.” Preserve analytical reasoning and decision rationale, not private hidden reasoning. Do not include credentials or unnecessary personal data.

If the session must end before all work is complete, deliver an updated partial pack with exact completed and pending status. At final completion, reconcile the pack against the actual delivered files and results. Provide the master pack as its own downloadable MD file in addition to any ZIP.

## 2. Seller interviews and document preferences

The user chose qualitative seller interviews because access to a large seller sample is unlikely. Recruitment will be **convenience sampling**, including whatever mixed seller types are reachable. Confirmed guide requirements:

- Entirely Indonesian, conversational and polite, addressing respondents as **Kak**.
- Approximately 30 minutes, eight core questions plus selective optional probes.
- DOCX with two columns: questions/probes and typed answers. Cells expand as answers are entered.
- Respondent fields: code/name optional, product type, selling channels, time selling, approximate monthly orders, interview date/time, and interviewer.

- User added a respondent photo area for documentation. Final guide includes space to insert a photo, caption/date/location/photographer fields, and separate optional photo permission. Interview, recording, and photo permissions are distinct.
- No team logo or institution identity was supplied; none should be invented.

Validation themes: seller total economics; value of channel demand relative to fees; actual changes in stock/effort/ad spend/channel allocation rather than account closure alone; payout predictability and cash flow; returns/logistics/listing/dispute recovery; differentiated assortment and customer continuity; discovery/ad economics; and print-on-demand fit, launch barriers, workable terms, and incremental versus substituted products.

Ask about actual recent events first. Introduce PoD only after current business experience. Do not persuade sellers who reject the concept. Distinguish payout after platform deductions from profit after all costs, and stated interest from adoption. The buyer survey cannot establish seller economics or production-partner feasibility.

Final timing:

- 0–2 opening/consent.
- 2–4 business background.
- 4–8 economics of a representative recent order.
- 8–12 latest change in channel focus, or reasons for staying.
- 12–17 material operating problem and resolution.
- 17–21 discovery and purchase journey/marketing.
- 21–23 recent product-launch decision.
- 23–28 PoD concept and conditions for trying/rejecting.
- 28–30 highest-priority change and close.

## 4. Prototype computation and Monte Carlo correction

The user clarified that this is a competition prototype with predetermined scenarios and explicit assumptions, but **heatmaps and numerical consequences should genuinely be calculated**. The user then challenged the assistant's statement that Monte Carlo was unnecessary.

**Authoritative correction:** frontend-only Monte Carlo is feasible and desired for consideration. “No production model” does not mean a static screenshot or fake numerical outputs. A browser engine can calculate capacity, costs, allocation, financial effects, and thousands of seeded uncertain worlds. A Web Worker can keep computation off the main UI thread. Runtime must be measured rather than promised.

Distinguish:

- Deterministic operating rules and financial formulas.
- Random draws for uncertain demand, cost, travel time, capacity loss, etc.
- Policy search across allocations/capacity choices.
- A selected-world twin replay versus a multi-world heatmap summary.

Use fixed seeds/matched worlds and fresh finalist draws. Example proposed experiment sizes were approximately 100 policies × 1,000 worlds for screening and 10,000 fresh worlds for finalists. These are **planning suggestions**, not achieved runs or strict requirements. Do not claim every heatmap cell received 10,000 runs without actual execution. Compare against matching counterfactual demand, include structural uncertainty, and do not label assumed-distribution success frequency as empirical confidence.

A lightweight surrogate trained on simulation results was discussed as an optional way to accelerate interactive previews, with measured approximation error. It is not required, implemented, or validated. It would approximate the simulator rather than establish real Nexora behaviour.

Jev was researched as TypeSafe's structured-decision model. Its proposed role is narrow exception classification/prioritisation; numeric consequences and feasibility belong to code/optimisation. Speed or vendor calibration claims do not establish logistics decision quality. No API calls, actual latency/cost benchmarks, or integration occurred here. **The current prototype must not depend on Jev:** use local rules/scripted responses labelled Demo response. A real deployment could evaluate it separately with a rule-based comparator.
